title: Progressive Consumption Bands: predictive soft-cap + auto-topup flow for committed customers
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem statement: Customers on committed plans (reserved credits / Dedicated customers) want predictable invoices but also occasional headroom for traffic spikes. Current hard caps or simple overage billing either cause dropped requests or unexpected bill shock. This feature introduces progressive consumption bands (multiple soft-cap tiers) with an optional predictive auto-topup flow that purchases short-term credits or reallocates burst budget automatically while keeping invoice transparency and explicit customer controls.

This ticket is the PRD + acceptance criteria for the pricing and billing behavior, billing line items, and console visibility required to ship the feature. It defines deterministic rules so engineering and finance can implement meter changes and invoice formatting without ambiguity.
goals: Provide 3 configurable soft-cap tiers (soft-1, soft-2, soft-3) that gradually reduce non-critical request throughput instead of hard-blocking
Enable an opt-in predictive auto-topup that buys short-duration credits when forecasted consumption will exceed the next 48 hours of committed capacity
Ensure billing transparency: invoices show soft-cap usage, auto-topup events, and daily consumption breakdowns to reconcile charges
Support per-environment and per-route priority weights so critical endpoints remain available under soft-caps
scope_in: Metering changes: new counters for soft-tier usage and auto-topup quantity
Console UX: per-tenant chart for band utilization, recent auto-topups and their costs
Billing: invoice line items for 'soft-band consumption' and 'auto-topup purchase' with clear unit pricing
API/SDK: new /usage endpoints that return current band state and remaining soft credits
scope_out: Self-serve plan creation flows (this ticket only modifies existing plans to support bands)
Marketplace billing integration; invoices will use existing invoice export format (no changes to payment rails)
requirements: Config model: plans must expose three band thresholds as percentages of committed capacity (e.g., 100-120% soft-1, 120-150% soft-2, 150-200% soft-3)
Priority routing: requests are tagged with a priority label (critical, standard, bulk) and soft-cap throttling must preserve a user-configurable percentage of capacity for 'critical' traffic
Auto-topup policy: customers may opt-in to 'predictive' or 'manual' auto-topup. Predictive uses a 48h horizon forecast; manual requires customer confirmation via Console or billing webhook
Unit pricing: soft-band token price and auto-topup temporary rate are configurable per-plan; default markup over base overage rate is 15% for predictive-topups
Invoice details: each auto-topup must create a distinct invoice line with: start/end timestamps, quantity purchased, unit price, and SKUs linking back to plan definitions
Metering windows: billing snapshot granularity remains daily; however console shows 1h resolution for band utilization charts
Safety guards: auto-topup cap (percentage of monthly committed tokens) default 25%; admin can raise for enterprise agreements
Accounting: unused auto-topup credits expire at month boundary and appear as credit adjustments on next invoice
billing_acceptance_criteria: When a tenant in plan X consumes 110% of monthly committed tokens and soft-1 is configured for 100-120%, system should throttle 'bulk' priority by 40% while maintaining 'critical' at 95% availability; no request returns 429 for 'critical' endpoints unless full system outage

If predictive forecast indicates the tenant will cross soft-2 within 36 hours and customer has predictive auto-topup enabled, the system creates a pre-authorized auto-topup reservation and invoices a 'prepaid topup' line; sample test: committed=100M tokens, forecasted need=130M -> auto-topup purchase=30M at configured rate
Manual opt-in path: when predictive flag disabled, Console shows a banner with a one-click 'purchase burst credits' action; click results in immediate invoice line and meter credit in <60s
Billing line item tests: invoices must include SKU, quantity, unit price, taxed amount and a human-readable description matching 'Auto-topup (predictive) — Feb 2026 — 30,000,000 tokens'

Edge case: if auto-topup purchase would exceed safety guard (25% cap) by requested amount, system purchases only up to cap and sends an admin alert; acceptance: purchase quantity <= cap and alert posted to tenant notifications and ops channel
Refund handling: unused auto-topup credits expire and appear as a negative adjustment on the next invoice; acceptance: create adjustment record referencing original auto-topup invoice ID

Meter reconciliation: daily usage export includes columns soft_band, band_duration_seconds, auto_topup_id and remaining_auto_credits; engineers must be able to reconcile sample tenant consumption across daily export and invoice lines within ±0.1%
Observability: a rollout test where 5% of tenants have predictive enabled must surface any billing spikes in Console 'billing anomalies' dashboard within 10 minutes of the event
metrics: % of overage events handled by soft-bands vs hard blocks (target: 90% handled by soft bands)
Average invoice variance (expected vs actual) for tenants with predictive auto-topup (target <5%)
Rate of customer-initiated refunds tied to auto-topups (target <0.5% of auto-topup volume)
Time from predictive signal to invoice creation (target <5 minutes)
Reconciliation error between billing export and metering export (target <0.1%)
risks: Finance/Accounting complexity: adding interim invoice lines and credit expiry adds reconciliation work. Mitigation: staging export and 2-week dry-run with no charges
Customer confusion: many line items could create bill shock. Mitigation: default predictive-topup OFF and clear console messaging
Over-provisioning: predictive model may over-forecast; mitigation: conservative forecasting default, throttling fallback and safety guard cap
Implementation drift: different teams (metering, billing, console) must align on schemas. Mitigation: contract-first schema and integration test suite
